title: How the Science of Habits Can Help Us Keep Our New Year’s Resolutions, with Wendy Wood, PhD

sentences.en: Welcome to January and our first episode of 2021.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到一月，这是我们2021年的第一期节目。

sentences.en: By now, some of you are a few days into a new diet, determined to finally lose 10 pounds.
sentences.zh: 现在，你们中的一些人已经开始执行新饮食计划几天了，决心最终减掉10磅。

sentences.en: Or maybe you downloaded a new language learning app and you're planning to resurrect your high school French or Spanish.
sentences.zh: 或者，也许你下载了一个新的语言学习应用程序，正计划重拾高中时学的法语或西班牙语。

sentences.en: Perhaps you're working on the household budget so you can find new ways to save money.
sentences.zh: 也许你正在制定家庭预算，以便找到省钱的新方法。

sentences.en: Whatever your goals are for this year, many of us are brimming with good intentions right now.
sentences.zh: 无论你今年的目标是什么，我们许多人现在都充满了良好的意愿。

sentences.en: But by February, it's likely that many of us will have reverted to our old ways.
sentences.zh: 但到了二月，我们很可能又会回到老样子。

sentences.en: Why do so few New Year's resolutions stick?
sentences.zh: 为什么很少有新年决心能坚持下去？

sentences.en: And more broadly, why is it so difficult to make lasting behavioral changes?
sentences.zh: 更广泛地说，为什么做出持久的行为改变如此困难？

sentences.en: Is it just a lack of willpower or is something else at play?
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是因为缺乏意志力，还是有其他因素在起作用？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: If you enjoy Speaking of Psychology, the conversation doesn't have to stop when the podcast is over.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢《心理学谈话》，那么播客结束时，对话不必就此停止。

sentences.en: Get unlimited access to hundreds of videos about the latest in psychology for just one low price by registering for access to APA's 2020 virtual convention.
sentences.zh: 注册参加美国心理学会2020年虚拟大会，只需支付一笔低廉的费用，即可无限次观看数百个关于心理学最新进展的视频。

sentences.en: Start with some of our selected videos featuring psychology's biggest names discussing topics such as racism, stigma, and COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 先从我们精选的一些视频开始，这些视频由心理学界的大咖们讨论种族主义、污名化和新冠疫情等话题。

sentences.en: Or use our on-demand library to explore any psychological or behavioral topic.
sentences.zh: 或者使用我们的点播库来探索任何心理学或行为学主题。

sentences.en: Go to convention.apa.org slash podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 请访问convention.apa.org斜杠podcaSt。

sentences.en: That's convention.apa.org slash podcaSt.
sentences.zh: That's convention.apa.org slash podcaSt.

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Wendy Wood, a professor of psychology and business at the University of Southern California.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是南加州大学心理学和商业教授温迪·伍德博士。

sentences.en: She has spent decades studying how people form habits and how habits drive our behavior.
sentences.zh: 她花了数十年时间研究人们如何形成习惯，以及习惯如何驱动我们的行为。

sentences.en: In her recent book, Good Habits, Bad Habits, The Science of Making Positive Changes That Stick,
sentences.zh: 在她最近的著作《好习惯，坏习惯：养成持久积极改变的科学》中，

sentences.en: She explains how understanding the science of habits can help us make the lasting changes to our behavior that we want.
sentences.zh: 她解释了理解习惯科学如何帮助我们实现我们想要的持久行为改变。

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, Dr. Wood.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到《心理学谈话》，伍德博士。

sentences.en: Oh, thank you.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢。

sentences.en: It's great to be here, Kim.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里，金。

sentences.en: Your research has found that a full 43% of our behavior is habitual, a number that might surprise some people.
sentences.zh: 你的研究发现，我们43%的行为是习惯性的，这个数字可能会让一些人感到惊讶。

sentences.en: How did you arrive at that statistic and what kinds of behaviors count as habits?
sentences.zh: 你是如何得出这个统计数据的？什么样的行为算作习惯？

sentences.en: When I started doing research on habits, I thought, like most people, that habits were just the simple little things we do,
sentences.zh: 当我开始研究习惯时，像大多数人一样，我以为习惯只是我们做的一些简单的小事，

sentences.en: like brushing our teeth or putting on our seatbelt when we get into a car.
sentences.zh: 比如刷牙，或者上车时系好安全带。

sentences.en: But we did some research where we actually followed people and beeped them once an hour and had them tell us what they were doing and what they were thinking.
sentences.zh: 但我们做了一些研究，实际上跟踪了人们，每小时给他们发一次信号，让他们告诉我们他们在做什么，在想什么。

sentences.en: And then we later had them tell us how often they do whatever they were doing in that circumstance.
sentences.zh: 后来我们让他们告诉我们，在那种情况下，他们做某事的频率是多少。

sentences.en: And what we found, this is where the 43% comes in, is that about 43% of the behaviors that people reported were ones that they were doing almost every day in the same circumstance,
sentences.zh: 我们发现——这就是43%的由来——人们报告的行为中，约有43%是他们在相同情况下几乎每天都在做的事情，

sentences.en: and they were doing them without thinking about what they were doing.
sentences.zh: 而且他们在做这些事时并没有思考自己在做什么。

sentences.en: So there's some non-conscious process there that is guiding our actions because we don't have to consciously think about them.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里有一种非意识过程在引导我们的行动，因为我们不需要有意识地去思考它们。

sentences.en: And that's the definition of habit, is habits are behaviors that you form through repetition
sentences.zh: 这就是习惯的定义，习惯是通过重复形成的行为，

sentences.en: that you repeat relatively automatically, so you don't have to think about them when you do them.
sentences.zh: 你相对自动地重复这些行为，所以当你做这些事时，你不需要去思考它们。

sentences.en: 43% is a big number.
sentences.zh: 43%是一个很大的数字。

sentences.en: But, you know, an awful lot of our behavior is pretty repetitive, much more than we realize, because when we repeat things, we're not thinking about what we're doing.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我们大量的行为是非常重复的，比我们意识到的要多得多，因为当我们重复做某事时，我们并没有在思考我们在做什么。

sentences.en: We're just doing it.
sentences.zh: 我们只是在做而已。

sentences.en: And we're typically doing it in the same way that we did before.
sentences.zh: 而且我们通常是以和以前相同的方式在做。

sentences.en: So that's sort of the way most of us live our lives.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们大多数人生活的方式。

sentences.en: And if you had to really think about all of these things, it would slow you down, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你真的必须思考所有这些事情，那会拖慢你的速度，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, like, you know how to drive a car.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，比如，你知道怎么开车。

sentences.en: That's habitual.
sentences.zh: 那是习惯性的。

sentences.en: It's not as if you have to open the door, get in, turn the key, you know, whatever the movements are.
sentences.zh: 并不是说你必须思考开门、坐进去、转动钥匙，你知道，无论动作是什么。

sentences.en: You don't think about them, right?
sentences.zh: 你不会去想它们，对吧？

sentences.en: That's what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在谈论的。

sentences.en: Yep, that's it.
sentences.zh: 是的，就是这样。

sentences.en: If you did have to think about it, it would be exhausting, because you'd be constantly having to think about, what is the next thing I do now after I've done that?
sentences.zh: 如果你真的必须去思考它，那会让人筋疲力尽，因为你必须不断地思考：做完这件事后，我现在要做的下一件事是什么？

sentences.en: And that kind of decision-making is just most of us, none of us can do it.
sentences.zh: 而那种决策过程，我们大多数人，没有人能做到。

sentences.en: Our brains are not set up for that.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑不是为了那个而设置的。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk about New Year's resolutions since it's that time of the year.
sentences.zh: 好吧，既然现在是一年中的这个时候，我们来谈谈新年决心吧。

sentences.en: Many of us have made some resolutions, and many of us will fail to keep them.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人都制定了一些决心，而我们许多人也将无法坚持下去。

sentences.en: Now, in your book, you talk about how people think it's just a matter of having enough willpower, but that's not it, right?
sentences.zh: 现在，在你的书中，你谈到人们认为这只是意志力是否足够的问题，但事实并非如此，对吧？

sentences.en: What are we doing wrong?
sentences.zh: 我们做错了什么？

sentences.en: Well, starting with your first question about how much of our behavior is habitual,
sentences.zh: 嗯，从你的第一个问题开始，关于我们有多少行为是习惯性的，

sentences.en: habits are a memory system that is very slow to change.
sentences.zh: 习惯是一种改变非常缓慢的记忆系统。

sentences.en: After you repeat a behavior over and over in the same way, say you may drink coffee in the morning, and you probably make it in the same way each morning,
sentences.zh: 在你以同样的方式反复重复一种行为后，比如你可能早上喝咖啡，而且你可能每天早上都用同样的方式冲泡它，

sentences.en: and I'm guessing that when you stand in front of your coffee maker in the morning, you're not asking yourself how to do it or what to do.
sentences.zh: 我猜当你早上站在咖啡机前时，你并没有问自己该怎么做或做什么。

sentences.en: It just happens automatically.
sentences.zh: 它只是自动发生了。

sentences.en: You're not even asking yourself if you want coffee this morning.
sentences.zh: 你甚至没有问自己今天早上是否想喝咖啡。

sentences.en: If you're a coffee drinker, that's what you do.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个喝咖啡的人，这就是你会做的事。

sentences.en: So, since so much of our behavior is like that,
sentences.zh: 所以，既然我们这么多的行为都是那样的，

sentences.en: and it's part of this habit memory system that learns slowly over time and only changes slowly if you want to alter the behavior,
sentences.zh: 而且它是这种随着时间缓慢学习的习惯记忆系统的一部分，如果你想改变这种行为，它也只能缓慢地改变，

sentences.en: it's very hard to alter our habits once we've formed them.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们形成了习惯，就很难改变它们。

sentences.en: In fact, many of us think that we should be able to make a decision, right?
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们许多人认为我们应该能够做出决定，对吧？

sentences.en: I am going to lose weight this year.
sentences.zh: 我今年要减肥。

sentences.en: I'm going to make more friends this year.
sentences.zh: 我今年要多交朋友。

sentences.en: I'm going to be nicer to my family, my partner this year.
sentences.zh: 我今年要对我的家人、我的伴侣更好一些。

sentences.en: I'm going to save more money.
sentences.zh: 我要存更多的钱。

sentences.en: All of those great New Year's resolutions that you mentioned in the introduction.
sentences.zh: 所有这些你在介绍中提到的伟大的新年决心。

sentences.en: But the problem is, is that so many of those behaviors are habits, and that memory sticks.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，这些行为中有太多是习惯，而那种记忆是根深蒂固的。

sentences.en: It sticks long after our decisions to change have fallen away, and we've given up.
sentences.zh: 即使在我们改变的决定消失、我们放弃之后，它依然存在。

sentences.en: So, habit memory is great because it gets us that coffee every morning in the way we like it.
sentences.zh: 所以，习惯记忆很棒，因为它让我们每天早上都能喝到我们喜欢的咖啡。

sentences.en: But it's also a challenge because it is resistant to change.
sentences.zh: 但它也是一个挑战，因为它具有抗拒改变的特性。

sentences.en: And when we want to change, it's very hard.
sentences.zh: 当我们想要改变时，这非常困难。

sentences.en: So, are some types of New Year's resolutions more likely to succeed than others?
sentences.zh: 那么，某些类型的新年决心是否比其他类型更容易成功？

sentences.en: How can we craft resolutions that we're going to be more likely to be able to keep?
sentences.zh: 我们怎样才能制定出更有可能坚持下去的决心？

sentences.en: There's actually some great data on this, and it's not my data.
sentences.zh: 实际上有一些关于这方面的好数据，而且不是我的数据。

sentences.en: It was done with people who had formed New Year's resolutions and then were contacted three months later to see which ones they stuck with.
sentences.zh: 它是针对那些制定了新年决心的人进行的，三个月后联系他们，看看他们坚持了哪些。

sentences.en: And people were asked to rate two things.
sentences.zh: 人们被要求对两件事进行评分。

sentences.en: One is how much fun it would be.
sentences.zh: 一是它会有多有趣。

sentences.en: Two, how enjoyable they'd find the resolution.
sentences.zh: 二是他们会觉得这个决心有多令人愉快。

sentences.en: That was one thing they rated.
sentences.zh: 这是他们评分的一件事。

sentences.en: And a second is how life-changing or how important the resolution would be.
sentences.zh: 第二是这个决心会有多改变生活或有多重要。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's why we make resolutions.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这就是我们制定决心的原因。

sentences.en: We make resolutions because they change our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们制定决心是因为它们改变了我们的生活。

sentences.en: So, you'd think that people would stick with the ones that were more life-changing and important.
sentences.zh: 所以，你会认为人们会坚持那些更改变生活、更重要的决心。

sentences.en: But that's not true.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Instead, they stuck with the ones that were more fun, more enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们坚持的是那些更有趣、更令人愉快的决心。

sentences.en: And part of the reason for that is because our habits form when we repeat a behavior and get a reward for that.
sentences.zh: 这其中的部分原因是，我们的习惯是在我们重复一种行为并从中获得奖励时形成的。

sentences.en: That reward triggers a release of dopamine in our neural systeMs.
sentences.zh: 那种奖励会触发我们神经系统中多巴胺的释放。

sentences.en: And that dopamine works to tie together what we're doing into habit memories so that we start to consolidate and learn to repeat that particular behavior.
sentences.zh: 而多巴胺的作用是将我们正在做的事情与习惯记忆联系起来，这样我们就开始巩固并学会重复那种特定的行为。

sentences.en: So, figuring out what you can do as a resolution that is, to you, enjoyable is going to be very important in whether you actually stick with it.
sentences.zh: 因此，找出你能做出的、对你来说令人愉快的决心，对于你是否真的能坚持下去将非常重要。

sentences.en: Probably much more important than most of us realize.
sentences.zh: 可能比我们大多数人意识到的要重要得多。

sentences.en: How long does it take for something to become a habit?
sentences.zh: 一件事情变成习惯需要多长时间？

sentences.en: I know there's been some data regarding, you know, what sounds like a pretty short period of time for something to become a habit.
sentences.zh: 我知道有一些关于——你知道，听起来变成习惯的时间相当短——的数据。

sentences.en: But I think you have found something that's a little bit surprising in that area.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你在那个领域发现了一些有点令人惊讶的事情。

sentences.en: So, because habit memories are learning systems, habits are part of a learning system, things that are easier to learn, you pick them up faster than things that are more difficult.
sentences.zh: 所以，因为习惯记忆是学习系统，习惯是学习系统的一部分，更容易学习的事情，你比那些更困难的事情学得更快。

sentences.en: So, there's not a single number of repetitions that you have to do in order to form a habit.
sentences.zh: 所以，没有一个单一的重复次数是你必须做才能形成习惯的。

sentences.en: That said, there are data suggesting that a simple health behavior like taking a walk after dinner or eating fruit with your lunch, that those can take,
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，有数据表明，像晚饭后散步或午餐吃水果这样简单的健康行为，它们可能需要，

sentences.en: those kinds of simple behaviors can take, oh, maybe two months, three months to start to become a habit in the sense that they start to feel automatic.
sentences.zh: 这类简单的行为可能需要，哦，也许两个月、三个月才能开始变成习惯，因为它们开始感觉自动了。

sentences.en: So, you don't really have to make a conscious decision and struggle anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以，你真的不需要再做出有意识的决定并挣扎了。

sentences.en: Instead, they're things that you just do automatically.
sentences.zh: 相反，它们是你自动做的事情。

sentences.en: So, give yourself two to three months of repeating things as often as possible and you should be able to form a habit.
sentences.zh: 所以，给自己两到三个月的时间，尽可能多地重复这些事情，你应该就能形成习惯。

sentences.en: Now, some habits that we now have have taken really years to settle in to become habits for basically for the population.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们现在拥有的一些习惯，实际上花了几年时间才沉淀下来，成为基本上属于大众的习惯。

sentences.en: I'm thinking of wearing seatbelts or smoking less or not smoking at all.
sentences.zh: 我想到的是系安全带，或者少抽烟，或者根本不抽烟。

sentences.en: Can you talk about how they became habitual but why it took as long as it did?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈它们是如何变得习惯性的，但为什么花了那么长时间吗？

sentences.en: Well, smoking has an interesting history because around the middle of the last century, we started to learn that smoking was really bad for us.
sentences.zh: 嗯，吸烟有一段有趣的历史，因为在上个世纪中叶左右，我们开始了解到吸烟对我们真的很不好。

sentences.en: And there was the landmark 1965 Surgeon General's report outlining exactly all of the health risks of smoking.
sentences.zh: 1965年具有里程碑意义的卫生局局长报告概述了吸烟的所有健康风险。

sentences.en: And that had an effect, some effect on people's behavior, but not a whole lot.
sentences.zh: 那产生了一些影响，对人们的行为产生了一些影响，但不是很大。

sentences.en: I mean, smoking is a habit.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，吸烟是一种习惯。

sentences.en: It's also addictive.
sentences.zh: 它也是成瘾性的。

sentences.en: Nicotine is highly addictive.
sentences.zh: 尼古丁具有高度成瘾性。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 然而，美国政府实施了几项帮助人们控制这些习惯的政策。

sentences.en: government, though, put into place several policies that helped people control those habits.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是他们在公共场所禁止吸烟。

sentences.en: And one was that they banned smoking in public places.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们让人们吸烟变得更困难了。

sentences.en: So, they made it more difficult for people to smoke.
sentences.zh: 所以，你每次拿出一支烟时都必须开始思考，这是我可以吸烟的地方吗？

sentences.en: So, you have to start thinking every time you take out a cigarette, is this a place where I can smoke?
sentences.zh: 他们对香烟征税，所以购买它们变得更难了。

sentences.en: They put taxes on cigarettes, so it was harder to buy them.
sentences.zh: 他们把香烟从商店货架上拿走，所以实际上购买它们变得更难了。

sentences.en: They took the packets off store shelves so that it was harder to actually purchase them.
sentences.zh: 你必须去问柜台后面的人要你吸的特定品牌和类型。

sentences.en: You have to go ask somebody behind a counter for the particular brand and type that you smoke.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情都给这种行为施加了我们所说的摩擦力，使它变得更困难，使它变得更需要思考。

sentences.en: All of these things put what we call friction on the behavior and made it more difficult, made it more difficult, made it more thoughtful.
sentences.zh: 所有这些因素加在一起，将吸烟率从上世纪中叶的50%降低到了现在的约15%，

sentences.en: And that cut smoking rates, all of these things together, cut smoking rates from 50%, which is what it was the middle of last century, to about 15% now,
sentences.zh: 目前只有约15%的美国人吸烟，这太棒了。

sentences.en: only about 15% of American smoke currently, which is wonderful.
sentences.zh: 这是一个令人惊叹的、积极的健康干预成功案例。

sentences.en: It's an amazingly positive success story for a health intervention.
sentences.zh: 但它也让我们个人对如何控制不想要的习惯有了一些洞察。

sentences.en: But it also gives us some insight personally about how to control unwanted habits.
sentences.zh: 我之前说过，你的决定不会像你的习惯记忆那样持久。

sentences.en: I said earlier that your decisions aren't going to last as long as your habit memories.
sentences.zh: 所以，做出决定和运用意志力是一个很好的短期修复方法，但不太可能持续足够长的时间让你真正改变你的行为。

sentences.en: And so, making decisions and exerting willpower is a good short-term fix, but is not likely to persist long enough for you to actually change your behavior.
sentences.zh: 然而，有帮助的是给那个你想改变的习惯施加摩擦力，让它变得更需要思考，让它变得更困难，这会给你一些对它的控制权。

sentences.en: What can help, though, is putting friction on that habit that you want to change, make it more thoughtful, make it more difficult, and that gives you some control over it.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种常见的想法。

sentences.en: But this is a common idea.
sentences.zh: 营销界有一句谚语，当你走进一家商店时，视线水平就是购买水平，这意味着你容易看到的东西就是你最可能购买的东西。

sentences.en: There's a saying in marketing that when you go into a store, eye level is buy level, meaning what you can see easily is what you're most likely to buy.
sentences.zh: 他们把便宜的东西放在你脚边或很高的地方，把他们想让你买的东西放在视线水平。

sentences.en: They put the cheap things way down by your feet or way up high, put the things that they want you to buy at eye level.
sentences.zh: 那就是摩擦力。

sentences.en: That's friction.
sentences.zh: 它在市场上有效。

sentences.en: It works in the marketplace.
sentences.zh: 它在网上也有效。

sentences.en: It works online.
sentences.zh: 所以，亚马逊有一段时间垄断了这个一键购买应用程序。

sentences.en: So, Amazon, for a while, had a monopoly on this one-click purchasing app.
sentences.zh: 两次点击你就会失去客户。

sentences.en: Two clicks and you lose customers.
sentences.zh: 一次点击，你在销售东西方面就更成功。

sentences.en: One click, you're more successful at selling things.
sentences.zh: 摩擦力确实是我们自身行为的一种强大力量，而且它不是我们所认识到的那种力量。

sentences.en: Friction is really a powerful force on our own behavior, and it's not one that we recognize.
sentences.zh: 当我们说“我要改变我的行为”时，它不是我们大多数人会想到的那种力量。

sentences.en: It's not one that most of us think of when we say, I'm going to change my behavior.
sentences.zh: 我们向内看。

sentences.en: We go inward.
sentences.zh: 我们专注于我们意识到的事情，我们知道的事情，也就是意志力和决定。

sentences.en: We focus on the things that we're aware of, the things we know, which is willpower and decision.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果我们专注于环境中的摩擦力，尝试让我们想做的事情更容易，让我们不想做的事情更难，我们会更成功。

sentences.en: We'd be more successful, though, if we focus on friction in our environment, trying to make the things that we want to do easier, things that we don't want to do harder.
sentences.zh: 所以，摩擦力更多地带有负面含义。

sentences.en: So, friction has more of a negative connotation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我就是这样看待它的。

sentences.en: I mean, that's how I would see it.
sentences.zh: 所以，它是让事情变得更困难而不是更容易。

sentences.en: So, it's making it more difficult instead of easier.
sentences.zh: 我有点在想，我知道在你的书中你写到了你的表亲，对吧，她定期在Facebook上宣布她减肥的意图，

sentences.en: I'm kind of thinking in terms of, I know in your book you wrote about your cousin, right, who periodically announces on Facebook her intention to lose weight,
sentences.zh: 这不可避免地在一段时间后失败了。

sentences.en: which inevitably fails after a while.
sentences.zh: 这是我们许多人都会做的事情。

sentences.en: And this is something that a lot of us do.
sentences.zh: 我们告诉我们的朋友和家人我们的决心，试图让自己承担责任。

sentences.en: We tell our friends and family about our resolutions in an effort to hold ourselves accountable.
sentences.zh: 所以，那种，你所期待的是正强化吗？

sentences.en: So, does that sort of, what you're expecting is positive reinforcement.
sentences.zh: 所以，那种，你所期待的是正强化吗？

sentences.en: Will that help people more than friction, which sounds more negative, like taking things away, making it harder for you to do something as opposed to easier.
sentences.zh: 这是否比“摩擦力”更能帮助人们？“摩擦力”听起来更负面，像是剥夺，让你做某事变得更难，而不是更容易。

sentences.en: The habit that you want to change becomes more difficult.
sentences.zh: 你想改变的习惯变得更难了。

sentences.en: The habit that you want to instill becomes easier, right?
sentences.zh: 你想培养的习惯变得更容易了，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, friction really has two sides.
sentences.zh: 所以，摩擦力确实有两面性。

sentences.en: You're absolutely right in the way you described it.
sentences.zh: 你刚才的描述非常准确。

sentences.en: It is a resisting force that you can use to help control behaviors you don't want.
sentences.zh: 它是一种阻力，你可以利用它来帮助控制你不想要的那些行为。

sentences.en: But it's also a force that reduces resistance, right?
sentences.zh: 但它也是一种能减少阻力的力量，对吧？

sentences.en: You can reduce that resistance, make it a driving force for behaviors that you do want.
sentences.zh: 你可以减少那种阻力，使其成为你想要的行为的驱动力。

sentences.en: Your question about sharing your resolutions with other people, that's helpful.
sentences.zh: 关于与他人分享你的决心，这确实有帮助。

sentences.en: I mean, other people can help us meet our goals, certainly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，其他人当然可以帮助我们实现目标。

sentences.en: And having a great support network is good for our mental health.
sentences.zh: 拥有一个强大的支持网络对我们的心理健康很有好处。

sentences.en: It's something we should all strive for.
sentences.zh: 这是我们所有人都应该努力去做的。

sentences.en: But if you're trying to change your own behavior, setting up some sort of public accountability is only minimally successful.
sentences.zh: 但如果你试图改变自己的行为，建立某种公开的问责制，其成功率其实很低。

sentences.en: The research that has been done on accountability suggests that it has great short-term effects.
sentences.zh: 关于问责制的研究表明，它在短期内效果显著。

sentences.en: The problem is, longer term, it's harder to keep accountability influencing your behavior in the way you want it to.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，从长远来看，很难让问责制持续以你想要的方式影响你的行为。

sentences.en: So, accountability is something like our decisions and our willpower that works in the short run, but not so much in the long run.
sentences.zh: 所以，问责制就像我们的决策和意志力一样，在短期内有效，但在长期内效果并不理想。

sentences.en: Let me give you an example of how friction can work for us, not just as a resisting force, but as something that can help us do the things we want to do.
sentences.zh: 让我给你举个例子，说明摩擦力如何为我们所用，它不仅是一种阻力，还能帮助我们完成想做的事情。

sentences.en: There was a great study done with our cell phones, tracking cell phones.
sentences.zh: 有一项很棒的研究是通过追踪手机进行的。

sentences.en: And you know that your cell phone is being tracked all the time for all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 你知道你的手机一直因为各种原因被追踪着。

sentences.en: This particular study tracked hundreds of thousands of cell phones to see how far people, and their cell phones, traveled to a paid fitness center.
sentences.zh: 这项特殊的研究追踪了数十万部手机，看看人们及其手机去付费健身中心的距离有多远。

sentences.en: So, how far they traveled to a gym.
sentences.zh: 也就是他们去健身房的路程有多远。

sentences.en: And what they found is that people who travel about three and a half miles on average went to a gym five times a week.
sentences.zh: 研究发现，平均路程在三英里半左右的人，每周会去健身房五次。

sentences.en: But people who traveled over five miles went only once a week on average.
sentences.zh: 但路程超过五英里的人，平均每周只去一次。

sentences.en: So, if you're trying to get yourself to exercise more, you probably aren't thinking that much about how far your gym is.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想让自己多锻炼，你可能并没有太在意健身房离你有多远。

sentences.en: You're probably thinking all the reasons why you should exercise, trying to convince yourself, get your willpower to make yourself go.
sentences.zh: 你可能在想所有你应该锻炼的理由，试图说服自己，调动意志力让自己去运动。

sentences.en: But one of the important factors that influences whether we actually go is how easy or difficult it is.
sentences.zh: 但影响我们是否真的去运动的一个重要因素，是这件事有多容易或多困难。

sentences.en: Can you find a gym that's close by your work so that after work you can easily stop by there?
sentences.zh: 你能找到一家离你工作地点很近的健身房，这样下班后就能顺便去吗？

sentences.en: Or close by a store that you usually go to, your grocery store, close by your house?
sentences.zh: 或者离你常去的商店、杂货店或家很近？

sentences.en: That matters.
sentences.zh: 这很重要。

sentences.en: That reduces the friction, makes it easier to go, and then you're much more likely to actually follow through on your resolution.
sentences.zh: 这减少了摩擦力，让去健身房变得更容易，这样你就更有可能真正坚持你的决心。

sentences.en: You've also written about how times of discontinuity are particularly conducive to habit change.
sentences.zh: 你还写过关于“不连续时期”如何特别有利于习惯改变的文章。

sentences.en: People are more likely to change their habits when they're in the middle of a life change, like a move or a breakup that disrupts many of their old routines.
sentences.zh: 当人们处于生活变动中时，比如搬家或分手，打破了许多旧的日常习惯，他们更容易改变自己的习惯。

sentences.en: Now, because of COVID-19, most of us have been living a good year, about a year in a state of disruption and upended routines.
sentences.zh: 现在，由于新冠疫情，我们大多数人已经过了一年左右生活被打乱、日常习惯被颠覆的状态。

sentences.en: Does that mean that this is a particularly good year for making life changes because we're all in a state of flux?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着今年特别适合做出生活改变，因为我们都处于一种变动状态中？

sentences.en: And will the changes we're making now be more likely to stick when life returns to normal, whatever that is?
sentences.zh: 而且，当生活恢复正常（无论那意味着什么）时，我们现在做出的改变是否更有可能持续下去？

sentences.en: Yeah, this is hard to know.
sentences.zh: 是的，这很难说。

sentences.en: We have seen some pretty broadly shared changes in people's lives.
sentences.zh: 我们确实看到人们的生活发生了一些相当普遍的变化。

sentences.en: Some of them are good, right?
sentences.zh: 其中一些是好的，对吧？

sentences.en: So people are eating out less often.
sentences.zh: 比如人们外出就餐的次数减少了。

sentences.en: So diets have become slightly healthier since the pandemic started.
sentences.zh: 所以自疫情开始以来，饮食变得稍微健康了一些。

sentences.en: But we're moving less.
sentences.zh: 但我们的活动量减少了。

sentences.en: So there's been less exercise and people have, on average, tended to gain weight.
sentences.zh: 所以锻炼变少了，人们平均体重往往有所增加。

sentences.en: We've picked up new hobbies.
sentences.zh: 我们培养了新的爱好。

sentences.en: So there's increasing interest in gardening.
sentences.zh: 比如对园艺的兴趣增加了。

sentences.en: And people have started cooking.
sentences.zh: 人们也开始做饭了。

sentences.en: So there are now memes about sourdough starters and all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 所以现在到处都是关于酸种面包发酵剂之类的梗。

sentences.en: Will people continue doing those things after the pandemic restrictions are over?
sentences.zh: 疫情限制结束后，人们还会继续做这些事情吗？

sentences.en: That's less clear because we're all going to get back to our old lives with our old environments and forces in our lives that we had habits for before the pandemic started.
sentences.zh: 这一点不太明确，因为我们都会回到旧的生活中，回到旧的环境，回到那些在疫情开始前我们就已经习惯了的力量中。

sentences.en: And one possibility is that as we launch ourselves back into picking up our lives as they left off a year ago, we're going to start picking up the same habits as well.
sentences.zh: 一种可能性是，当我们重新开始一年前中断的生活时，我们也会开始重新拾起同样的习惯。

sentences.en: Because those habit memories are still there.
sentences.zh: 因为那些习惯记忆依然存在。

sentences.en: So they're still there to be activated.
sentences.zh: 所以它们依然在那里，等待被激活。

sentences.en: It is an opportunity for us to think about what we want to bring from the pandemic and what we want to change in our old behavior.
sentences.zh: 这是一个让我们思考的机会：我们想从疫情期间保留什么，又想改变哪些旧行为。

sentences.en: So it's an opportunity for us to think, well, how do we keep gardening if we enjoy that?
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个让我们思考的机会，比如，如果我们喜欢园艺，该如何保持下去？

sentences.en: How do we keep cooking at home a bit more?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何继续多在家做饭？

sentences.en: How do we keep doing things with our family more maybe than we did before the pandemic?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何继续像疫情期间那样，多花时间与家人在一起？

sentences.en: These are opportunities for us to think about behavior change and which ones we want to keep, which ones we don't.
sentences.zh: 这些都是让我们思考行为改变的机会，思考哪些是我们想保留的，哪些是不想的。

sentences.en: But don't be surprised if you find yourself just falling back sort of mindlessly into your old routines because that's your habit memory.
sentences.zh: 但如果你发现自己又不自觉地回到了旧的日常习惯中，也不要感到惊讶，因为那是你的习惯记忆。

sentences.en: It takes actually changing context, as you said,
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这确实需要改变环境，

sentences.en: disrupting the context that activate your habits in order to provide that sort of window of opportunity to make new decisions and to establish new habits.
sentences.zh: 打破那些激活你习惯的环境，才能提供一个做出新决定、建立新习惯的窗口期。

sentences.en: It's interesting to think about it, though, in terms of, you know,
sentences.zh: 不过，换个角度思考很有意思，你知道，

sentences.en: so many of us are teleworking right now and our employers have become accustomed to that and realize that we can actually be more productive in some cases.
sentences.zh: 我们现在有很多人在远程办公，雇主们已经习惯了这一点，并意识到在某些情况下我们实际上效率更高。

sentences.en: So perhaps we won't be going back to our lives as we knew them before.
sentences.zh: 所以也许我们不会回到以前那种生活方式了。

sentences.en: And maybe some of these habits will stick.
sentences.zh: 也许其中一些习惯会保留下来。

sentences.en: So perhaps this is an area for future research for you, Dr. Wood.
sentences.zh: 所以这或许是你未来研究的一个领域，伍德博士。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: One thing I thought was interesting was a study that you published a few years ago on stress and habits.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有一点很有趣，就是你几年前发表的一项关于压力与习惯的研究。

sentences.en: And there's this idea that a lot of us have that when people are under stress, they do unhealthy things like stress eat.
sentences.zh: 我们很多人都有这种想法：当人们处于压力下时，他们会做一些不健康的事情，比如压力性进食。

sentences.en: But you found out that when people are stressed, they may actually double down on whatever their habits are, whether they're good or bad, healthy or unhealthy.
sentences.zh: 但你发现，当人们感到压力时，他们实际上可能会加倍强化他们原有的习惯，无论是好是坏，健康还是不健康。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that a little bit?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这一点吗？

sentences.en: Most of us think that when we're stressed, we're going to fall back into doing things that make ourselves comfortable.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人认为，当我们感到压力时，我们会退回到那些让自己感到舒适的事情上。

sentences.en: And most of those are bad habits.
sentences.zh: 而其中大多数是坏习惯。

sentences.en: We will watch too much TV.
sentences.zh: 我们会看太多的电视。

sentences.en: We'll surf the web.
sentences.zh: 我们会漫无目的地浏览网页。

sentences.en: We'll eat too much.
sentences.zh: 我们会吃得太多。

sentences.en: But in research that we've done and other people on stress and fatigue, feeling fatigued and overwhelmed, not having much decision-making capacity left,
sentences.zh: 但在我们和其他人关于压力和疲劳的研究中，感到疲惫和不知所措，没有多少决策能力了，

sentences.en: sort of the way you feel drained at the end of a hard day.
sentences.zh: 就像你在辛苦一天后感到精疲力竭的那种感觉。

sentences.en: When you're in those circumstances, you expect to fall back on bad habits because they're comforting.
sentences.zh: 当你处于那种情况下，你期望退回到坏习惯中，因为它们很舒服。

sentences.en: But what we found actually is that people fall back on good habits too.
sentences.zh: 但我们实际上发现，人们也会退回到好习惯中。

sentences.en: And the reason is this, that when you are stressed or when you're fatigued, you are not as able to control your behavior.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，当你感到压力或疲劳时，你控制自己行为的能力就会下降。

sentences.en: Executive control functions are sort of tapped.
sentences.zh: 执行控制功能被消耗了。

sentences.en: They are not able to control behavior in quite the same way.
sentences.zh: 它们无法以同样的方式控制行为。

sentences.en: And so without our decision-making capacity, we fall back on what we would typically do.
sentences.zh: 因此，在没有决策能力的情况下，我们退回到了我们通常会做的事情上。

sentences.en: And that typical could be something good, right?
sentences.zh: 而那种“通常”可能是件好事，对吧？

sentences.en: It could be that you work a whole lot and that's your habit.
sentences.zh: 可能你的习惯就是努力工作。

sentences.en: Or it could be that you exercise or go for long walks or call somebody who's a good friend that you can talk with and end up feeling better.
sentences.zh: 或者可能是锻炼、长距离散步，或者给一位可以倾诉的好友打电话，最后感觉好多了。

sentences.en: All of those things are beneficial habits that you're more likely to repeat when you're stressed and fatigued than when you're not.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是有益的习惯，当你感到压力和疲劳时，你比平时更有可能重复这些行为。

sentences.en: It makes perfect sense that there would be that pattern if you understand how habits work.
sentences.zh: 如果你了解习惯是如何运作的，那么出现这种模式就完全说得通了。

sentences.en: But it doesn't always fit our understanding of our own behavior.
sentences.zh: 但这并不总是符合我们对自己行为的理解。

sentences.en: And part of that is we don't notice the good habits that we engage in.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是，我们没有注意到我们所从事的好习惯。

sentences.en: In fact, most of us think we are acting in ways that are consistent with our intentions.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们大多数人认为我们的行为与我们的意图是一致的。

sentences.en: So we must have wanted to do that all along.
sentences.zh: 所以我们一定是一直想那样做。

sentences.en: We must work out when we're feeling stressed because we know that that's going to help relieve the stressful experience.
sentences.zh: 我们一定是在感到压力时去锻炼，因为我们知道这有助于缓解压力体验。

sentences.en: Instead of recognizing, oh, that's my habit and that's why I fell back on it when I was stressed.
sentences.zh: 而不是意识到，哦，那是我的习惯，这就是为什么我在压力大时会退回到那个习惯。

sentences.en: People underestimate their good habits and they tend to focus too much on their bad ones.
sentences.zh: 人们低估了自己的好习惯，而倾向于过多关注坏习惯。

sentences.en: And that's why we know so much more about bad habits than we do about good ones.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们对坏习惯的了解远多于对好习惯的了解。

sentences.en: What can your work, your science, tell us about some of the issues related to COVID-19, like getting people to wear masks and keep their physical distance?
sentences.zh: 你的工作和科学研究能告诉我们关于新冠疫情相关的一些问题吗？比如如何让人们戴口罩并保持身体距离？

sentences.en: I mean, these are habits that we're trying to instill in people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些是我们试图在人们身上培养的习惯。

sentences.en: And we're having a lot of pushback in some parts of our country.
sentences.zh: 而且我们在我国的一些地区遇到了很大的阻力。

sentences.en: What can the science of studying habits tell us that policymakers could use to convince people to do the good things?
sentences.zh: 习惯科学能告诉我们什么，让政策制定者用来劝说人们做正确的事情？

sentences.en: So part of the reason for the pushback, I think, is political as much as anything.
sentences.zh: 我认为，阻力的一部分原因在很大程度上是政治性的。

sentences.en: And it's based on a misunderstanding of the severity of the virus.
sentences.zh: 而且它是基于对病毒严重性的误解。

sentences.en: But there are absolutely things that policymakers can do to help people stay safer.
sentences.zh: 但政策制定者绝对可以采取一些措施来帮助人们保持更安全。

sentences.en: And we do know at this point that the virus is as much a behavioral science challenge as it is a medical challenge.
sentences.zh: 我们现在知道，这种病毒既是一个行为科学挑战，也是一个医学挑战。

sentences.en: We can control the virus by wearing masks and keeping physical distance from others.
sentences.zh: 我们可以通过戴口罩和与他人保持身体距离来控制病毒。

sentences.en: We can also control it through vaccines.
sentences.zh: 我们也可以通过疫苗来控制它。

sentences.en: There's two routes.
sentences.zh: 有两条途径。

sentences.en: Both are important.
sentences.zh: 两者都很重要。

sentences.en: Estimates are that with the best vaccines, we're still not going to be able to get back to normal until we start bringing the virus levels down in the broader population.
sentences.zh: 据估计，即使有最好的疫苗，在我们开始降低广大人口中的病毒水平之前，我们仍然无法恢复正常。

sentences.en: At least we're not going to be able to do that very quickly.
sentences.zh: 至少我们无法很快做到这一点。

sentences.en: So using the idea of friction, you want to make it easy for people to wear masks.
sentences.zh: 所以利用摩擦力的概念，你想让人们戴口罩变得容易。

sentences.en: And something that retailers, stores, communities can do is make them free and available when people need them.
sentences.zh: 零售商、商店和社区可以做的一件事是，在人们需要时免费提供口罩。

sentences.en: So when you walk into a store, there should be a bunch of masks, disposable masks available that people can use.
sentences.zh: 所以当你走进商店时，应该有一堆口罩，一次性口罩供人们使用。

sentences.en: So they don't have to remember to bring their own.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就不必记得带自己的口罩了。

sentences.en: Make it easy for people to keep using masks.
sentences.zh: 让人们更容易持续使用口罩。

sentences.en: Individuals themselves can do things to make it easy to remember to use a mask.
sentences.zh: 个人也可以做一些事情，让自己更容易记住戴口罩。

sentences.en: Hang it in your car.
sentences.zh: 把它挂在车里。

sentences.en: Hang it by your door so that it just becomes part of your habitual everyday leaving the house.
sentences.zh: 把它挂在门口，这样它就成了你出门习惯的一部分。

sentences.en: You pick up your keys, you put on your mask, you leave.
sentences.zh: 你拿起钥匙，戴上口罩，然后出门。

sentences.en: Same thing with physical distancing.
sentences.zh: 保持身体距离也是一样。

sentences.en: Help people do it on a regular basis.
sentences.zh: 帮助人们定期做到这一点。

sentences.en: So the marks that you see in pavements and stores about how far to stay away from other customers, from other people, they're great.
sentences.zh: 所以你在人行道和商店里看到的关于与他人保持多远距离的标记，它们很棒。

sentences.en: They're very helpful.
sentences.zh: 它们非常有帮助。

sentences.en: They remind people what to do and they make it the norm so that we're much more likely to just learn to do this and keep doing it in the future.
sentences.zh: 它们提醒人们该做什么，并使其成为常态，这样我们更有可能学会这样做，并在未来继续保持。

sentences.en: There are a lot of things that people can do to apply behavioral science knowledge to help themselves change this behavior so that they're able to keep themselves and others safe.
sentences.zh: 人们可以做很多事情来应用行为科学知识，帮助自己改变这种行为，从而能够保护自己和他人。

sentences.en: Last question.
sentences.zh: 最后一个问题。

sentences.en: Have you applied your research in your own life?
sentences.zh: 你是否在自己的生活中应用了你的研究？

sentences.en: Do you make New Year's resolutions and can you keep them?
sentences.zh: 你会制定新年决心吗？你能坚持下去吗？

sentences.en: I don't make New Year's resolutions, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我不制定新年决心。

sentences.en: But, you know, like everybody else, I try to change my behavior.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，像其他人一样，我也试图改变自己的行为。

sentences.en: And given the knowledge that we've all gained in the past couple of decades about habits and how they work,
sentences.zh: 鉴于我们在过去几十年里对习惯及其运作方式的了解，

sentences.en: it is possible to apply that in your own life to help with behavior change challenges.
sentences.zh: 将其应用到自己的生活中来帮助应对行为改变的挑战是可能的。

sentences.en: So one of my favorite studies was done with eating and it was done with people sitting in a room with two bowls of food.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的实验之一是关于饮食的，它是让人们坐在一个房间里，面前放着两碗食物。

sentences.en: Some of them had a bowl of apples right in front of them, sliced apples, and then buttered popcorn was there in front of them, but they had to reach for it.
sentences.zh: 有些人面前放着一碗苹果，切好的苹果，然后面前还有黄油爆米花，但他们必须伸手去拿。

sentences.en: Other people had the buttered popcorn right in front of them and the apple slices they had to reach for them.
sentences.zh: 另一些人面前放着黄油爆米花，而苹果片则需要伸手去拿。

sentences.en: And what the researchers found is that people who had apple slices close by ate a third fewer calories than people who had the popcorn close by.
sentences.zh: 研究人员发现，苹果片放在手边的人比爆米花放在手边的人少摄入了三分之一的热量。

sentences.en: And it's not that they were less hungry or didn't like the popcorn.
sentences.zh: 并不是他们不饿或者不喜欢爆米花。

sentences.en: It's just having to reach for it was enough friction so that they were more likely to just eat the apples.
sentences.zh: 只是必须伸手去拿就构成了足够的摩擦力，所以他们更有可能直接吃苹果。

sentences.en: So when I go to the grocery store, I typically buy fruits and vegetables that are already prepared or cut up in some way.
sentences.zh: 所以当我去杂货店时，我通常会买已经处理好或切好的水果和蔬菜。

sentences.en: And they're a little bit more expensive, but I know that I'm more likely to eat them if I do that.
sentences.zh: 它们稍微贵一点，但我知道如果我这样做，我更有可能吃它们。

sentences.en: So if I'm trying to clean up my diet, if I feel like there's some need to do that,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我试图改善饮食，如果我觉得有必要这样做，

sentences.en: I will fill my refrigerator with fruit and vegetables all ready to eat so that when I open it, that's what's there.
sentences.zh: 我会把冰箱装满准备好即食的水果和蔬菜，这样当我打开冰箱时，看到的就是这些。

sentences.en: And I make sure that there are things that I like.
sentences.zh: 而且我确保里面有我喜欢的东西。

sentences.en: So I don't buy things that are just because they're good for me.
sentences.zh: 所以我不会仅仅因为它们对我有好处就买那些东西。

sentences.en: I try to get things that are rewarding and easy.
sentences.zh: 我尽量买那些既有回报又容易获取的东西。

sentences.en: And with those two keys, it makes it much easier to change your behavior.
sentences.zh: 有了这两个关键点，改变行为就容易多了。

sentences.en: And we all have to do that.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都必须这样做。

sentences.en: We all have periods where we eat too much, where we don't exercise enough, where we might be a little short with our spouse.
sentences.zh: 我们都有吃得太多、锻炼不足、或者对配偶态度不够好的时候。

sentences.en: Trying to figure out ways to make it easier to do the right thing is a good approach and works better than willpower because it's more long lasting.
sentences.zh: 设法让做正确的事情变得更容易是一种很好的方法，而且比意志力更有效，因为它更持久。

sentences.en: Well, this has been some great advice.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些建议真是太棒了。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.en: And I'm much more determined now to keep my resolution.
sentences.zh: 现在我更有决心去坚持我的新年目标了。

sentences.en: So thank you for joining us today, Dr. Wood.
sentences.zh: 那么，非常感谢伍德博士今天能来参加我们的节目。

sentences.en: It's been really a pleasure talking to you.
sentences.zh: 与您交谈真是太愉快了。

sentences.en: No, it's good fun.
sentences.zh: 不，这很有趣。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at www.speakingofpsychology.org or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 或您获取播客的任何平台收听《心理学谈话》往期节目。

sentences.en: If you have comments for future podcasts, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 如果您对未来的播客有任何建议，可以发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》由李·韦纳曼制作。

sentences.en: Our sound editor is Chris Kondayan.
sentences.zh: 我们的音频编辑是克里斯·康达扬。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯，代表美国心理学会向您致意。
